General.Description:
The Congo River is the second longest river in Africa and the deepest river in the world. Its basin contains the second largest tropical rainforest on Earth, more species of freshwater fish than any other river system, and some of the most biodiverse and least-studied ecosystems on the planet. It also flows through a region of extraordinary political complexity, where conservation and conflict have been inseparable for decades.

Carlos Reinholt is a wildlife biologist and writer who spent fourteen months travelling the length of the Congo River by a combination of cargo boat, dugout canoe, and walking, documenting wildlife, speaking with fishermen, conservationists, rangers, and villagers, and trying to understand the relationship between this vast ecosystem and the communities that depend on it.

River of Stars is the account of that journey — a travel narrative of genuine literary quality that is equally concerned with the ecological and the human. Reinholt writes the natural world with the trained eye of a scientist and the sensibility of someone who understands that a river is not merely a geographical feature but a fact of life for every person and creature in its basin.

Magnificent in scope and immensely readable. A great river book.
